correctness.rationale: At the 2N+1 equally spaced nodes, exact cardinal trigonometric interpolation expresses any normalized nodal-nonnegative p as a convex combination of translates of D_N. Convexity and translation invariance give negative mass at most (||D_N||_{L1(mu)}-1)/2=(2/pi^2)log N+O(1). For fixed K choose q=2K+1 grid phases near distinct q-th roots of unity; invertibility of the real Fourier moment matrix and small perturbation produce positive mass-one quadrature weights killing the first K complex moments. Their separated Dirichlet mixtures satisfy all nodal/moment constraints and retain the full L1 logarithmic contribution because overlaps are uniformly bounded away from singular neighborhoods. Strictly positive analytic Poisson mixtures have identical low moments, project to polynomials converging in L2 to those extremizers as the Poisson parameter tends to 1, and nonexpansiveness of convex Hilbert projection plus L1 Lipschitz of negative-part mass realizes the lower bound. All quantifiers fix K and allow f depending on N. The limiting coefficient follows from analysis, not finite numerical slopes.

value.rationale: The result quantifies the sharp worst-case failure of grid-only positivity in a natural moment-constrained Fourier spectral method. It shows that preserving any fixed number of low Fourier moments cannot reduce the leading logarithmic off-grid negative mass, even for strictly positive analytic inputs selected at each resolution. This is a substantive conservation-versus-positivity limitation, rather than a restatement of classical Dirichlet L1 growth.

limitations: Only one-dimensional odd-grid collocation, fixed K>=1 low Fourier moments, normalized mass one, and asymptotic N to infinity.
Inputs realizing the supremum vary with N; no fixed analytic input shows divergence.
No exact finite-N constrained optimum and no claim for growing K or polynomial momentum/energy moments.
